skills.name: ontotect
skills.short_description: Route and execute ontology engineering workflows
skills.description: Systematic ontology engineering for designing, constructing, reviewing, repairing, optimizing, refactoring, validating, documenting, and governing ontologies, vocabularies, taxonomies, knowledge graphs, semantic models, and mappings. Use when the request spans ontology stages or when Ontotect should choose the appropriate workflow.
skills.instruction: If no arguments were supplied, execute `help`. Otherwise preserve any explicit Ontotect command in the arguments; when none is explicit, execute `router`.

skills.name: ontotect-help
skills.short_description: Learn what Ontotect is and how to use it
skills.description: Explain Ontotect, its ontology-engineering modes, lifecycle stages, invocation forms, evidence boundaries, and the best first command. Use when a user is new to Ontotect or asks how to start.

skills.name: ontotect-router
skills.short_description: Route ontology work to the right mode and stage
skills.description: Route an ontology-engineering request to the appropriate Ontotect mode, lifecycle entry stage, evidence path, authorization boundary, and next gate. Use when the desired outcome is clear but the correct workflow is not.

skills.name: ontotect-status
skills.short_description: Report ontology work state and the next gate
skills.description: Reconstruct and report the current Ontotect work state, including mode, stage, artifacts, decisions, evidence, blockers, and next gate. Use when ontology work is already in progress and must not be advanced or modified.

skills.name: ontotect-build
skills.short_description: Design, construct, or extend an ontology
skills.description: Design, construct, or extend an ontology through explicit requirements, competency questions, reuse analysis, conceptualization, formalization, implementation, verification, and release gates. Use for new ontology work or authorized extensions.

skills.name: ontotect-review
skills.short_description: Review an ontology without silently changing it
skills.description: Perform an evidence-driven, read-only review of an ontology, vocabulary, taxonomy, mapping, shapes graph, query set, or release bundle. Use to identify semantic, logical, structural, validation, documentation, tooling, and governance defects without silently repairing them.

skills.name: ontotect-repair
skills.short_description: Repair a reproduced ontology defect
skills.description: Repair a reproduced ontology defect with a minimal authorized change, protected semantic invariants, regression evidence, and migration notes when needed. Use after a defect has been localized and file modification is explicitly authorized.

skills.name: ontotect-optimize
skills.short_description: Optimize measured ontology cost or complexity
skills.description: Optimize an ontology or ontology toolchain against a measured reasoning, query, validation, loading, modularity, or maintenance objective while preserving declared semantics. Use when a baseline and measurable optimization target exist.

skills.name: ontotect-refactor
skills.short_description: Refactor ontology structure safely
skills.description: Refactor ontology structure under an explicit preservation contract for identifiers, entailments, competency questions, mappings, imports, shapes, and downstream behavior. Use for modularization, naming cleanup, pattern extraction, or structural simplification that is not intended to change meaning.

skills.name: ontotect-validate
skills.short_description: Validate ontology evidence without redesigning it
skills.description: Execute and interpret ontology validation evidence such as parsing, profile checks, reasoning, competency queries, SHACL, graph diffs, documentation checks, or release tests. Use when the requested checks are known and redesign is outside scope.

skills.name: ontotect-govern
skills.short_description: Govern ontology ownership and change
skills.description: Define or review ontology ownership, authority, identifier policy, change control, deprecation, mappings, provenance, maintenance, and decision records. Use when the problem is organizational or lifecycle governance rather than only formal modeling.

skills.name: ontotect-release
skills.short_description: Evaluate ontology release readiness
skills.description: Evaluate and prepare an ontology release disposition from integrated semantic, validation, migration, governance, documentation, and approval evidence. Use for release readiness; remote publication still requires separate explicit authority.

skills.name: ontotect-stage
skills.short_description: Select one ontology lifecycle stage
skills.description: Run or plan one named Ontotect lifecycle stage while preserving its prerequisites and stop conditions. Use with charter, reuse, conceptualize, formalize, implement, verify, or release when the user wants explicit stage control.
skills.instruction: Execute `stage <stage>`, taking the stage name from the first argument. Valid stages are `charter`, `reuse`, `conceptualize`, `formalize`, `implement`, `verify`, and `release`.

skills.name: ontotect-charter
skills.short_description: Frame ontology purpose, scope, and acceptance
skills.description: Frame an ontology project by defining purpose, users, scope, non-goals, competency questions, constraints, roles, and acceptance evidence. Use at lifecycle Stage A before reuse analysis or formal modeling.

skills.name: ontotect-reuse
skills.short_description: Assess ontology reuse, import, and mapping
skills.description: Assess candidate ontologies and vocabularies for direct reuse, import, module extraction, specialization, mapping, or justified new definition. Use at lifecycle Stage B after the ontology contract is clear.

skills.name: ontotect-conceptualize
skills.short_description: Build a precise ontology conceptual model
skills.description: Develop terms, definitions, examples, counterexamples, categories, identity criteria, taxonomy, and relations independently of implementation syntax. Use at lifecycle Stage C for conceptual ontology analysis.

skills.name: ontotect-formalize
skills.short_description: Choose semantics and formalize ontology commitments
skills.description: Select the semantic stack, OWL profile, IRI and module policy, axioms, constraints, assumptions, and query contracts for an ontology. Use at lifecycle Stage D after conceptual commitments are sufficiently clear.

skills.name: ontotect-implement
skills.short_description: Implement a tested ontology vertical slice
skills.description: Implement an ontology in small, reviewable vertical slices connecting terms, axioms, constraints, examples, competency queries, and tests. Use at lifecycle Stage E after the formalization contract is established.

skills.name: ontotect-verify
skills.short_description: Integrate ontology verification evidence
skills.description: Integrate syntax, logical, profile, competency-query, SHACL, semantic-diff, documentation, domain-review, and operational evidence. Use at lifecycle Stage F to determine whether earlier ontology commitments hold.

skills.name: ontotect-stage-release
skills.short_description: Complete the ontology lifecycle release gate
skills.description: Complete lifecycle Stage G by classifying semantic change, preparing migrations and release artifacts, confirming governance and approvals, and producing a release disposition. Use when explicit lifecycle-stage control is required; this differs from the broader release mode entry.
